title: Rails
notes: The application that rails new generates, with every framework and default gem loaded, on Puma with 3 threads in one process. Every page sets a session cookie; nothing is compressed.
details: The application `rails new` generates with Rails 8.1 and nothing taken out: every framework loaded (rails/all), Propshaft, importmap with Turbo and Stimulus, SQLite with Solid Cache, Solid Queue and Solid Cable configured (no database is opened), Bootsnap, and the generated layout (csrf_meta_tags, csp_meta_tag, stylesheet_link_tag, javascript_importmap_tags), ApplicationController (allow_browser versions: :modern) and production settings. The shop is added to it: /about is a controller action with an ERB view, rendered in the layout on each request since Rails has no build-time prerendering; the item page is an ERB view; the API uses render json. It is built with assets:precompile and bootsnap precompile and started from config.ru in production mode on one Puma server with 3 threads, the number in the generated config/puma.rb, and no workers. Every HTML response sets a session cookie (the forgery token of csrf_meta_tags) and carries an ETag. No response is compressed: a generated application leaves that to Thruster, a proxy in a second process, which is not run here. Differs from a generated application: Puma is started by the benchmark runner and not by `rails server`, so config/puma.rb is not evaluated and the pool is 0 to 3 threads where the file sets 3 to 3; RAILS_LOG_LEVEL=warn turns request logging off; SECRET_KEY_BASE comes from the environment and there is no credentials file; kamal, thruster and the development and test gems are not in the Gemfile; libvips is not installed, so Active Storage cannot make image variants (nothing asks it to); what a running application does not load (bin/, test/, db/, the Dockerfile, CI, the development and test settings) is left out. Gems are installed one at a time from gems.lock.json after their age and sha256 are checked, and loaded through Bundler with a frozen Gemfile.lock; seven of them (bigdecimal, bootsnap, msgpack, nio4r, puma, racc, websocket-driver) compile native extensions at install.
